text:
sarah: Quick sync — I'm running a 48h quantile sim for a Black Friday–style spike in eu-west1. Assumed 3x baseline QPS for a 2‑hour window. Need a concrete GPU-hours headroom plan and whether we prewarm or overprovision. Anyone have updated GPU-hour projections?

mo: Posted a draft from the traffic model, linking shortly. p95 burst ~12k GPU-hours total across region, p99 ~18k. That includes inference + KV cache memory headroom.

kevin: Are those numbers including Private/VPC footprints or just hosted? Private tenants usually add ~8% extra tail due to isolation.

mo: Good call — the draft is hosted-only. Add ~10% for private and ~5% extra for dedicated pools with pinned instances.

alice: From infra side: prewarm job takes ~45m to reach steady-state for most models due to session cache and kernel JIT. If we prewarm, we need to schedule ~1h earlier to be safe.

ravi-oncall: are there any network egress hotspots we should be worried about in eu-west1? Last time we saw NAT bottlenecks during the tail.

kevin: NAT was the limiting factor in the last run. We should route some training-mirroring traffic to eu-west2 and set up additional NAT gateways for the burst window.

capacity-bot: Forecast artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-capacity/1951234567/quantile_forecast.csv :white_check_mark:

sarah: Copying the CSV here for quick eyeballs so people don't have to click S3:```
quantile, gpu_hours
p50, 4200
p75, 7200
p90, 9800
p95, 12000
p99, 18000
```

alice: For prewarm vs overprovision math: prewarm cost = baseline x prewarm_duration x prewarm_instances; overprovision = full_window_extra_instances x full_window_duration. For a 2h window prewarm is usually cheaper if warmup < 30% of spike length.

mo: Quick calc we ran: prewarm (1h) ≈ 600 GPU-hours, overprovision full 2h ≈ 2400 GPU-hours. So prewarm saves ~1.8k GPU-hours in this scenario.

kevin: But prewarm also has operational complexity (orchestration + rollback). If networking/NAT fails, prewarmed instances could be useless. Need fallback: scale-to-fallback-model-variant (lighter quantized variant) across the cluster.

alice: Agreed. Recommend: 1) prewarm a 30% pool 1h prior, 2) keep autoscaler headroom to add 70% during spike, 3) enable variant-fallback to q4-micro if latency SLOs break.

ravi-oncall: I can run one dry-run prewarm tonight at 02:00 UTC. Will monitor NAT metrics and pod readiness. @alice can you own the orchestration runbook?

alice: Yep — I'll update the prewarm runbook and add the NAT checklist.

sarah: Cost tradeoff note for finance: if we prewarm we're paying ~600 GPU-hours vs 2400 if we cold start + ramp. But reserved capacity commitments for Dedicated could change marginal cost — mark as contingent.

mo: I'll update the capacity spreadsheet and add p50/p75/p90/p95/p99 columns and include Private multiplier. Link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1abcXYZ (updated row in the Capacity tab).

kevin: Also flag region fallback policy: if eu-west1 utilization > 85% for >5m, route 20% of new requests to eu-west2 and fall back model->q4-micro after 10m if error rate rises.

ravi-oncall: Dry-run scheduled at 02:00 UTC. I'll post logs and quick summary after. :thumbsup:

sarah: Perfect. Action items: mo update spreadsheet (owner), alice update prewarm runbook + NAT checklist (owner), ravi run dry-run (owner). We'll reconvene in #capacity-ops after the dry-run. Thanks all.
